- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for sustained positive sentiment.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >80) — add 3–8% buffer to prevent premature correction.
- Overshoot in early forecast horizon (1–7 days) — apply downward bias of 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- Mean-reversion bias in long-term (15–30 days) — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- Lagged sentiment decay: if sentiment drops below 0.3 after 5+ days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to reflect cooling momentum.
- Avoid overconfidence in high-sentiment spikes — cap forecast at 10% above recent peak if sentiment > 0.85.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high but price drops 5%+ in 3 days, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overreaction.
